summary.prose: Seven small, strictly serial tasks that move one optional field one hop and then render it where the document already puts it. Six of the seven are additive and revert by deleting what they added; the risk is concentrated in exactly one place — the bounded removal of the prose list beneath the document's own heading — which gets its own task, its own falsifier and a build-before-mutate ordering that keeps a construction throw from leaving a half-removed section. Behaviour changes exactly once and late, at a single call in renderContent, so reverting that one line restores today's surface with the types, the data path and the renderer all still in place. Every task closes on its own mutations rather than deferring them, because the path that fires on 630 of 634 ledger documents is the one where a test that passes by doing nothing proves nothing.

tasks.title: Carry the functional record from the host onto the existing docs-content message
tasks.summary: Append one optional field, `functionalDefinition`, to the docs-content variant of `HostToWebview` in protocol.ts, typed by INDEXING off `DocsContent['functionalDefinition']` rather than restating the record shape — so protocol → client → daemon stay one declaration deep and cannot drift. Then forward it in `openDoc` with a conditional spread placed beside the identical `degradation` spread already there, so an absent record stays an ABSENT KEY across the postMessage boundary rather than a key holding undefined. No new message type; this mirrors exactly how S001/t5 added `sections` and `degradation` to this same variant. Behaviour is unchanged after this task: the webview has no code that reads the field yet, and that is asserted rather than assumed.
acceptanceChecks: The docs-content variant in protocol.ts declares `functionalDefinition` as an indexed type off `DocsContent`, NOT as a restated record shape — a source assertion on the annotation form, so a future hand-copied shape fails the check.
Opening a document whose content carries a record posts a docs-content message whose `functionalDefinition` is the SAME object reference the client returned (no clone, no reshaping, no defaulting).
Opening a document whose content carries NO record posts a message where `'functionalDefinition' in payload` is false — an absent key, not an undefined value.
The fail-closed arm is unchanged: a content-fetch rejection still posts `blocked:true` and carries no record.

REPLACES the prior vacuous shell check (s3/t1): capture the emitted shell for a FIXED nonce before the change and assert the post-change shell is byte-identical to that captured baseline — a check that actually fails if t1 accidentally edits renderShell, the bootstrap or the mdStyle block.
Assert the webview bootstrap contains no reference to `functionalDefinition` after t1, so 'this task is data-only' is proved rather than assumed.

t1: a client returning no record posts a message with NO functionalDefinition key ('functionalDefinition' in payload === false)

tasks.title: Build the functional-requirements renderer as a third webview source string
tasks.summary: Add `DOCS_FR_SOURCE` beside DOCS_BODY_RENDERER_SOURCE and DOCS_SECTIONS_SOURCE, containing `renderFunctionalRequirements` — the first implementation of sc2's published `StructuredRenderer<FunctionalDefinition>`, returning `{ el }`. It constructs one discrete element per requirement, writes EVERY string with textContent and assigns no markup anywhere, carries id / statement / rationale, and preserves the record's doc-level-then-per-item-grouped-by-itemRef order rather than flattening it. Written in the same ES5-compatible style as its two siblings so it evaluates both inline in the webview and under `new Function` in tests. The record is treated as structurally untrusted: `requirements` not an array yields an empty container, a malformed entry is skipped while its well-formed siblings render, duplicates are preserved and an orphan `itemRef` falls into the same bucket the prose renderer uses. Also add the item CSS as one more fragment in the existing `mdStyle` concatenation, using `--it-*` variables only. Inert after this task — the string is defined and inlined but nothing calls it.
acceptanceChecks: An id containing `*`, `_`, backtick and `[` comes out of the DOM stub byte-identical to the record's value — the central falsifiable claim of this Story.
A statement containing `<script>alert(1)</script>` renders as text and creates no child element.
The renderer produces exactly one discrete element per requirement, asserted as a count against the record length and as distinct sibling nodes — not as a substring of the rendered text.
Doc-level requirements render before per-item ones, per-item requirements are grouped under their `itemRef`, and a group with no members produces no header.

ADDED (s3/t2a): a record with TWO entries sharing one FrId renders BOTH as distinct items in record order — neither dropped nor merged; a de-duplicating implementation must fail this check, because collapsing a duplicate would hide a real producer-side defect from the reviewer at the approval gate.

ADDED (s3/t2b): a `scope:'item'` entry whose `itemRef` is missing or empty is grouped under the SAME literal key the existing prose renderer uses (functional-definition.ts:99), asserted against that key rather than an invented one, so the two renderings of one record cannot disagree about where an orphan belongs.
A malformed record — `requirements` not an array, an entry that is not an object, an entry with a non-string id or statement — produces fewer items or an empty container and never throws.

The emitted shell still contains EXACTLY ONE `.innerHTML=` and it is still `el.innerHTML=marked.parse`; `DOCS_FR_SOURCE` itself contains no markup assignment, asserted with comments stripped before scanning.
Every item CSS rule references only `--it-*` variables — no `--sans`/`--fg-strong`/`--border`, which are undefined on this surface and would silently invalidate the declarations containing them.

CLOSING CONDITION (s3/t7): this task's own mutations are run here, not deferred — replacing textContent with a concatenated-markup assignment must turn the hostile-id check red, and flattening the doc/item grouping must turn the grouping check red.

tasks.title: Locate the document's functional-requirements section from the posted index
tasks.summary: Add `frAnchorSlug(sections)` to `DOCS_FR_SOURCE`: it scans the posted `SectionIndex` for the anchor whose TITLE ends with the format spine's heading text and returns that anchor's slug. Tail-matching rather than equality because the format engine prefixes a document-position-dependent number (`## 2. Functional requirements` on a DEF). It CONSUMES sc3's identity and mints none of its own — the returned value is a slug `deriveSectionIndex` already produced and `stampSlugs` has already written onto a heading element. A missing index, an empty index, an anchor without a title, or a renamed heading all return `undefined`, which is a SAFE no-match that routes the caller to the fallback placement rather than to a wrong substitution.
acceptanceChecks: An anchor titled `2. Functional requirements` matches, proving tail-matching under the engine's numeric prefix.
Matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace.
With two anchors whose titles both end in the heading text, the FIRST in document order is returned — never an ambiguous target.
An undefined index, an index with no anchors, and an index whose anchors lack titles each return `undefined` without throwing.

A document whose markdown contains the heading text inside a FENCED CODE BLOCK yields no match, because the posted index carries no anchor for it — confirming this task adds no second markdown scanner of its own.
docs-sections.ts is byte-identical to its pre-task state — this Story reads section identity and never edits its source.
CLOSING CONDITION (s3/t7): this task's mutation is run here — changing the match from title-tail to exact equality must turn the `2. Functional requirements` check red.

t3: a heading inside a fenced code block produces no anchor in the posted index and therefore no match

tasks.title: Place the rendered requirements — bounded in-section substitution, with a safe fallback
tasks.summary: Add `placeFunctionalRequirements(bodyEl, record, sections, bodyDegraded)` to `DOCS_FR_SOURCE`, returning `{ placed: 'in-section' | 'prepended' | 'none', degradation? }`. Three outcomes. ABSENT: an undefined record, an empty `requirements`, or a non-array yields `placed:'none'` with no element created and nothing removed. IN-SECTION: when the body rendered structurally and the resolved slug matches a heading element FOUND BY A LOOKUP SCOPED TO THE BODY CONTAINER, remove that heading's following siblings up to but NOT including the next heading element of ANY level (or the end of the container), and insert the built container in their place — leaving the heading, its text and its stamped slug untouched. PREPENDED: when the body degraded, the anchor does not resolve, or no heading carries the slug, insert the container as the body's first child instead; return a degradation ONLY when the body itself rendered fine, so no second notice stacks on an already-degraded document. On the degraded path the container the block lands in carries `.insrc-docs-plain`, whose `white-space:pre-wrap` and `word-break` would otherwise inherit into the items — the item rules must neutralise that explicitly (s3/t4). The sibling range is computed and the container fully built BEFORE the first removal, so a construction throw leaves the document intact. This task contains the only destructive operation in the Story.
acceptanceChecks: A body whose functional-requirements section is followed by two further sections keeps BOTH, and no heading element at any level is ever removed.
A functional-requirements section that is the LAST section removes to the end of the container without an off-the-end read or a throw.
After an in-section placement the section's heading element, its text and its stamped id are identical to before, so its chooser entry and anchor target still resolve.

After an in-section placement the body contains the built container and NOT the prose list that was there — the requirements are separated from surrounding prose by that prose being gone, not merely by styling.
A record that makes construction throw leaves the body COMPLETELY unmodified, with nothing removed — proving the build-before-mutate ordering rather than relying on a catch.
An undefined record yields `placed:'none'` with zero createElement calls and zero mutations of the body — asserted as the absence of DOM activity, not merely the absence of a visible section.

A degraded body yields `placed:'prepended'` with NO degradation returned (s1's notice already covers it); an unresolvable anchor on a well-rendered body yields `placed:'prepended'` WITH a degradation.
The slug lookup is scoped to the body container, so an element elsewhere on the surface sharing the id can never have its siblings deleted.

ADDED (s3/t4): the DEGRADED-path rendering is verified VISUALLY — render the real shell with a degraded body plus a record, screenshot it headless and READ the image — confirming the inherited `.insrc-docs-plain` white-space/word-break rules do not mangle the items on the one path where this block is the reviewer's only legible access to the commitments. A DOM stub cannot see this, and a pixel is never signed off on a green suite.

CLOSING CONDITION (s3/t7): this task's mutations are run here — deleting the absent-safe gate must turn the absent check red, and changing the removal bound to end-of-container must turn the bounded-removal check red.

tasks.title: Wire placement into the render pipeline — the single line that changes what a reviewer sees
tasks.summary: Call `placeFunctionalRequirements` from `renderContent`, positioned AFTER `stampSlugs` and BEFORE `renderSectionChooser` / `renderDegradationNotice`, wrapped in a backstop try/catch. The ordering is a correctness constraint, not a style one: `stampSlugs` pairs headings to anchors by title through a pointer that only advances, so mutating the tree first could mis-pair every later heading. Extend the notice precedence by one level — host-posted degradation, else the body renderer's, else placement's — so the reviewer is never shown two notices and never shown none when something went wrong. Concatenate `DOCS_FR_SOURCE` into the single nonce'd script after its two siblings. This is the only task that alters the rendered surface, and reverting this one call restores the shipped behaviour while leaving the data path, the types and the renderer in place.
acceptanceChecks: The placement call sits after `stampSlugs` and before the chooser and the notice in the emitted bootstrap.
The chooser's stamped-count gate behaves exactly as in S001 — placement adds and removes no heading element, so `stamped` means what it meant before.
Notice precedence: a host-posted degradation wins over a body degradation wins over a placement degradation, and exactly ONE notice is ever rendered.
A forced throw inside placement still renders the chooser, the notice, the open questions and the approve / request-changes controls — the backstop never costs the reviewer the rest of the surface.
Opening a document with no record produces a body byte-identical to the S001 rendering of the same markdown — the dominant path, proved as the main case.
The approve / request-changes path, the COMMENTABLE_KINDS gate and the blocked banner behave identically to before this Story.

ADDED (s3/t5): IDEMPOTENCE across messages — delivering two consecutive docs-content messages carrying the same record leaves exactly ONE constructed container with the same item count as a single delivery, and a third message carrying NO record leaves none; this proves the per-message rebuild CLEARS a previously placed block rather than merely not re-adding one. The pane really does post docs-content several times per session (open, boot ping, blocked approve, decision failure), so silent duplication here would reintroduce exactly what this Story removes.

CLOSING CONDITION (s3/t7): this task's mutations are run here — moving the placement call before `stampSlugs` must turn the ordering check red, and returning a degradation from the prepended-after-degraded path must turn the no-stacked-notice check red.

tasks.title: Rewrite the S001 contract test that asserted StructuredRenderer is implemented nowhere
tasks.summary: S001 exported `StructuredRenderer<T>` and pinned, by test, that no file among docs-review-panel.ts / docs-review-client.ts / docs-sections.ts / markdown-style.ts annotates a value with it. That assertion was written to hold only until the first implementer arrived, and this Story is that implementer. REWRITE it, do not delete it: the type is still exported, it is implemented in exactly ONE place — the functional-requirements renderer — and the other listed files still declare none. The replacement must still fail if a renderer appears somewhere unsanctioned. Record it in the commit as a deliberate, scoped narrowing, the same kind S001 made to the no-innerHTML assertion, never an incidental relaxation.
acceptanceChecks: The rewritten test still asserts `export type StructuredRenderer<` is present in docs-review-panel.ts.
It asserts exactly one implementation site and names it; introducing a second annotation in an unlisted file must turn it red — proved by actually adding one, not by reading the assertion.
docs-review-client.ts, docs-sections.ts and markdown-style.ts are still asserted to declare none.
The test's name and its comment state that this is a deliberate narrowing at the first implementer, so a later reader cannot mistake it for an eroded invariant.

tasks.title: Confirm the whole surface end to end and ship the extension build
tasks.summary: RE-SCOPED per s3/t7: the per-task mutations now close their own tasks, so t7 CONFIRMS rather than discovers. It re-runs the full mutation set as one sweep, runs the complete vscode-plugin suite (not just the docs-review file) and reports the real counts, runs tsc, verifies all three rendered states visually, measures the VSIX delta and checks the diff's scope. Then rebuild the extension bundle and VSIX and reinstall. There is NO daemon rebuild in this Story — nothing under src/ changes — and shipping the wrong artefact would make the change appear not to work.
acceptanceChecks: The full vscode-plugin sweep passes, with the ACTUAL pass/total counts reported rather than asserted.

The complete mutation set is re-run as a sweep and every mutation still turns its named test red; any that has gone green since its own task is reported as a regression in the test, not quietly re-fixed.

`tsc --noEmit` is clean for the plugin.
The VSIX size delta is measured and reported.
A scope check confirms the diff touches only protocol.ts, docs-review-panel.ts and its test file — no daemon file, no docs-sections.ts, no companion-slot groundwork for s3/s4.
The extension is rebuilt and reinstalled, and the report states plainly that no daemon rebuild was required.
